notes: Dispute over a building owner's covenant to repair a leased hotel (Irving House) between the owner and commercial hotel lessees after adjacent excavation damaged the walls; concerns landlord repair covenants generally, not the occupancy of lodgers/guests or its regulation.

Taxpayers sought to enjoin excise commissioners from granting liquor/inn licenses; court holds it lacks jurisdiction to restrain the commissioners' statutory discretion. The dispute is about liquor licensing and taxpayer standing, not the legal character of lodging or boarding.
Landlord-tenant ejectment dispute over a covenant to pay taxes and Croton water rents, forfeiture by re-entry, and equitable relief from forfeiture; no lodging or boarding issue.
Use-and-occupation action between an assignee-owner and tenants over an assigned commercial lease and a rent set-off claim; not about lodging or short-term letting.

Plaintiff's prior boarding-house keeping is mentioned only as the source of separate earnings in a dispute over whether property (a piano) is exempt from her husband's creditors under coverture law; the letting/boarding relationship itself is not adjudicated. New trial ordered on an unrelated procedural ground.
Dispute over the city's liability for use of a private pier in offal removal under a municipal contracting statute; no connection to lodging or boarding houses.

Nuisance/street-obstruction suit by the proprietor of an eating-and-lodging house against the city over market sheds blocking access to his premises; his lodging-house business is incidental identification, not the subject of adjudication.
Dispute over an assignee-for-creditors' personal liability for quarterly rent on a commercial lofts lease; no lodging/boarding issue.
Will/codicil construction case concerning executors' power of sale over a decedent's real estate; unrelated to short-term letting or lodging.
Summary dispossession proceeding for nonpayment of rent and the scope of equitable relief from a warrant of ejectment; concerns a commercial tenancy repair covenant, not lodging or boarding.

Attachment case turning on whether the defendant's hotel-room stays in New York City (as opposed to his family's home in Connecticut) made him a 'resident' for jurisdictional purposes; hotel boarding is incidental to the domicile analysis, not to the legal character of letting/lodging.
False-imprisonment action arising from a conviction for driving an unlicensed express wagon for hire under a municipal cartmen ordinance; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

Negotiable-instruments case on the diligence required to locate a note's maker before presentment; the maker's occupation as a boarding-house keeper is mentioned only to establish her whereabouts, not the legal character of boarding.

Married woman's separate-estate liability for furniture she purchased intending to use in keeping a boarding-house; the boarding-house use is incidental context for a coverture/separate-property holding, not an adjudication of the boarding relationship itself.
Dispute over which municipal officer had authority to permit or order removal of building materials obstructing a street; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

holding_summary: The court held that a house is treated as an inn, rather than a mere boarding-house, when it receives all who choose to visit without any prior agreement as to duration of stay or terms of entertainment. An innkeeper's strict liability for a guest's property lasts only while the guest relation continues, and ceases once the guest pays his bill and leaves with a declared intent not to return, after which any baggage left behind is at the guest's own risk. Because the trial court did not let the jury decide whether the guest relation had already ended when the trunk was lost, a new trial was ordered.

quotes.text: To charge a defendant, as an innkeeper, it is sufficient to prove, that he received, as guests, all who chose to visit his house, without any previous agreement, as to the duration of their stay, or the terms of their entertainment.

There may be a distinction between the liability of the keeper of an inn and of a mere boarding-house, where transient persons are not received at all, and none are received but for a certain time and upon certain terms. But it is not pretended that the defendant’s house was a mere boarding-house. It was a public house of entertainment for all who chose to visit it, which is the true definition of an inn.

That relation ceases, when the guest pays his bill and leaves the house, with the declared intention of not returning. In such a case it is at his own peril, we apprehend, that he leaves his baggage or other property behind him.

notes: Foundational innkeeper/boarding-house distinction case: relevant to the characterization taxonomy for short-term commercial lodging, though the dispute itself concerns baggage-bailment liability rather than the right to let or its regulation.
Trespass action over a rope/sign fixture attached to a roof, turning on a tenant's authority to license the act and resulting costs rule; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

Injunction against a soap factory as a nuisance to a nearby hotel (Irving House); the hotel is merely the injured neighboring business, and the case does not address the legal character of letting or lodging.
